ana: Heads-up — seeing a bunch of OOMs on GPU node groups and cluster-autoscaler is slow to add nodes. Anyone tuned CA flags specifically for GPU-heavy workloads? :thinking:

mikeg: Yup. We had to change the expander and increase scale-down timers. Short checklist:
- --expander=least-waste tends to pack GPUs better
- --scale-down-unneeded-time=30m for GPU groups
- --scale-down-delay-after-add=10m to avoid ripple deletions

sasha: can you paste the args you used? we run mixed pools (a100 / v100) so curious about heterogeneous behavior

mikeg: Sure — deployment args we run on prod CA (AWS):
```
--cloud-provider=aws 
--expander=least-waste 
--balance-similar-node-groups=true 
--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false 
--scale-down-unneeded-time=30m 
--scale-down-unready-time=20m 
--scale-down-delay-after-add=10m 
--scan-interval=20s 
--max-node-provision-time=15m
```
Note: for very heterogeneous fleets we sometimes flip balance-similar-node-groups to false so CA won't excessively favour one shape.

kevin: Practical tips: annotate long-running batch GPU groups with `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled: "true"` if you want them stable. Also use taints + tolerations for infra vs user jobs so tiny controller pods don't block scale-down.

sasha: we use MIG on a100. does least-waste still help if CA can't see fractional GPUs?

mikeg: Good point. CA needs node groups that map to the device slices for fractional packing. With MIG you can expose each slice as its own nodegroup or rely on device-plugin + scheduler. If you can't, `least-waste` might misestimate. For predictable behavior we switched to `--expander=most-pending` during high-traffic windows, then flip back.

autoscaler-bot: [alert] scale-up started for ng-gpu-a100-16 (3 -> 6) — reason: 12 pending pods, insufficient nvidia.com/gpu

ana: (typo) ana: thanks — will try least-waste + longer unneeded-time on staging first. anyone seen cost regressions with scale-down-unneeded-time=30m?

kevin: dev cluster cost up ~8% but production latency and pod wait times improved. Our compromise: per-nodegroup scale-down-disabled for stable groups + scheduled nightly consolidation jobs that drain low-util nodes after hours.

mikeg: Also consider CA flags: `--exclude-nodes-with-local-storage=false` if you want CA to consider nodes with local storage for deletion (be careful), and `--max-empty-bulk-delete=10` to let CA remove many useless empties quickly. Finally, bump `--max-node-provision-time` if cloud provider slowdowns cause phantom pending pods.

sasha: great, will test on staging and report. thanks! :thumbsup:
